title: GitHub - onatm/rustling: inference engine for inkling 2 mini
excerpt: inference engine for inkling 2 mini. Contribute to onatm/rustling development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
A fast local inference engine for Inkling 2 Mini on Apple silicon, written in Rust and built for coding agents. It serves an OpenAI-compatible API that Codex, aider and opencode can use as they would a hosted model.

It runs one model family and does not try to be general. That is what lets it do things a general engine does not: generate whole tokens in one GPU submission, keep processed prompts between requests and restarts, and copy runs of tokens the reply repeats from the conversation.

An earlier version of rustling chat running on an M1 Max with 64 GB. Watch it on asciinema.

Requirements

  • An Apple silicon Mac. Nothing else is supported: the engine is built around Metal and tuned on these chips.
  • Memory: 16.6 GB for the model, 1 to 5 GB for a conversation depending on its length, and up to 15 GB more while a long prompt is being processed. Measured on a 64 GB machine. 48 GB is comfortable; on 32 GB long prompts will push the model's own pages out of memory and slow down.
  • A Rust toolchain to build it.

Quick start

cargo install --path cli
rustling chat

The first run downloads Unsloth’s UD-Q4_K_M conversion (16.6 GB) to the Hugging Face cache, where other tools that use the Hub will find it too. rustling pull does only that, if you would rather fetch it ahead. A download that is interrupted starts again from the beginning; on an unreliable connection, hf download unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF Inkling-2-Mini-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf can resume, and rustling finds the file it leaves.

To serve it to other programs:

rustling serve
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}],
  "reasoning_effort": "low", "stream": true
}'

Usage

Chat

Run rustling chat from a project directory to ask questions about its files. The built-in agent runs the model locally and asks before reading or searching. Chat controls, sessions and MCP setup.

One reply

rustling generate "Write a function that reverses a linked list." --effort low
rustling generate "Write a haiku about rivers." --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.95 --seed 1
rustling generate "What is 17 * 23?" --temperature 0     # always the most likely token
rustling generate "Hello" --timing                       # where the time went

Server

rustling serve                                           # http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
rustling serve --port 9000 --host 0.0.0.0                # reachable from other machines
rustling serve --context 32768 --max-tokens 8192         # a larger window and longer replies
rustling serve --cache-gb 16                             # keep up to 16 GiB of processed prompts
rustling serve --cache-dir /Volumes/fast/rustling        # keep them somewhere else
rustling serve --no-cache-dir                            # keep them in memory only
rustling serve --no-reasoning                            # disable reasoning for every request
rustling serve --temperature 0.2 --top-p 0.9             # sampling for requests that do not set their own
rustling serve --log-level debug                         # also report progress through long prompts

The server's flags are defaults. A request sets its own temperature, top_p, top_k, seed, max_tokens and stop, and its reasoning effort, which is not a server flag:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Is 91 prime?"}],
  "reasoning_effort": "high", "max_tokens": 2000
}'

Reasoning comes back as reasoning_content, apart from the answer. GET /v1/models names the model and GET /health says the server is up.

Models

rustling pull                                            # fetch the default model ahead of time
rustling pull thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini            # the published checkpoint, 19 GB
rustling chat --model thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini    # run it
rustling serve --model ~/models/Inkling-2-Mini-Q4_K_M.gguf   # a file you already have
RUSTLING_MODEL=thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini rustling chat # or by environment

Without the GPU

rustling chat --backend cpu
rustling pull --draft && rustling chat --backend cpu --draft   # the draft model helps on the CPU

Coding agents

rustling serve provides streaming and tool calls through the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs. Configure Codex, aider or opencode.

Performance

On a 64 GB M4 Max with a 40-core GPU, rustling and llama.cpp ran the default Unsloth UD-Q4_K_M model on Metal. Each engine processed the same three prompts from scratch and generated 128 tokens per reply. The table shows medians across three runs per prompt, with greedy sampling and token copying disabled.

Measurement Engine 30 input tokens 2,413 input tokens 15,194 input tokens
Prompt time (s) rustling 0.5 12.3 73.9
Prompt time (s) llama.cpp 0.23 8.9 73.5
Generation (tokens/s) rustling 43.2 35.0 29.3
Generation (tokens/s) llama.cpp 37.1 35.7 30.7

In an agent session, rustling can reuse the part of the conversation it has already processed. Replies that repeat earlier text can also benefit from token copying. For run ranges, reproduction commands, and earlier M1 Max and M4 Max results with the LM Studio model, see the full benchmark results.

To try experimental split attention for long-context GGUF generation, build with cargo build --release --features split-attention and run target/release/rustling with a context window large enough for the prompt and reply (for example, serve --context 65536). It splits full attention across blocks of cached keys on the same GPU when generating one token with at least 32,768 visible keys. Prompt processing in large batches and speculative verification batches use the usual kernels. The different order of floating-point sums can change a reply.

Accuracy

The LM Studio Q4_K_M conversion was used for the measurements below. The GPU computes in a different arithmetic from the CPU, so each way of running it was scored against the published checkpoint: how often it picks the same most likely next token. The first row is the checkpoint itself in another, equally valid arithmetic, which shows how much disagreement is ordinary.

Source code (7,857 tokens) Agent session (12,891 tokens) The model's own writing in it
Checkpoint, float arithmetic 92.0% 87.0% 99.4%
Q4_K_M on the CPU 90.4% 83.7% 98.8%
Q4_K_M, GPU prompt path 90.6% 83.7% 98.8%
Q4_K_M, GPU token by token (last 2,600 tokens) 91.7% 93.5% 98.8%

Where the checkpoint gives its choice a probability of 90% or more, every row agrees with it at least 98% of the time, and on the model's own writing none of them ever disagreed. Perplexity is the same to within 2%. The conversion costs a point or two of agreement; running it on the GPU costs nothing measurable beyond that. tests/quality.rs reproduces this on text of your choosing.

Options

Everything has a default; these are the ones worth knowing. rustling <command> --help lists the rest.

Option Default What it does
--model unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF:Q4_K_M A model name, a .gguf file or a checkpoint directory. Names are downloaded when missing. Also $RUSTLING_MODEL.
--backend auto auto uses the GPU; cpu does not.
--context by chip, see below The most tokens a prompt and its reply may take together.
--max-tokens 4096 The longest reply.
--no-reasoning reasoning on Never let the model reason before answering. --effort none only shortens it.
--draft off Use the model's draft model to propose several tokens at a time. Only helps when generating on the CPU; with the GPU it is not used.
--no-copying copying on Stop proposing tokens copied from the conversation.
--cache-gb 8 How many GiB of processed prompts to keep, in memory and again on disk (serve).
--cache-dir, --no-cache-dir ~/.cache/rustling Where they are kept between runs, or not to keep them (serve).
--threads performance cores Worker threads for the CPU's share of the work.
--log-level info What is reported on stderr. Also $RUSTLING_LOG.

Context window

The model takes up to 1,048,576 tokens, but time grows with the context, so the default is sized for the chip: a prompt that fills the window should still be processed in about two minutes.

Chip Default window
M1 16,384
M2 20,480
M3 24,576
M4 32,768
M5 40,960
anything else 16,384

Only the M1 figure is measured (on an M1 Max). The others scale it by each generation's GPU and are estimates; measurements are welcome. --context sets any size you like. Each token of context costs 64 KB of memory, on top of a fixed 0.3 GB.

A prompt that does not fit is refused with a message saying so, and a reply stops when the window is full.

Logging

Logs go to stderr through tracing. At info, the server reports each request: the size of its prompt, how much of it was reused, how long the rest took and at what speed, and the reply's length and speed in tokens per second.

[3] 8 messages, 11 tools, 12891 prompt tokens
[3] prompt: 12615 tokens reused, 276 processed in 5.7s (48 tokens/s)
[3] reply: 164 tokens in 8.5s (19.4 tokens/s), stop; copied: 3 of 21 proposed tokens accepted in 10 rounds

--log-level debug adds progress through long prompts, warn keeps only problems, and off is silent.

Models

Model Size Notes
unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF:Q4_K_M 16.6 GB The default. Uses Unsloth’s Inkling-2-Mini-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf on Metal or CPU.
lmstudio-community/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF:Q4_K_M 17.5 GB The previous default, selectable with --model.
thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini 19 GB The published checkpoint in its own formats, on the CPU with GPU help for long prompts. About 10 tokens/s. The reference for accuracy.
thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research The variable-loop research checkpoint; --passes picks how many times the looped layers run.

The GGUF loader reads F32, BF16, NVFP4, Q4_K, Q5_0, Q5_K, Q6_K and Q8_0 tensors.

Limits

  • Text only. The model's vision tower is not implemented.
  • One request at a time; others queue.
  • Apple silicon only. There is no CUDA or Vulkan backend, and none is planned.
  • A 4-bit conversion is a lossy copy of the checkpoint. See Accuracy for how close.

How it works

docs/internals.md describes each part and what it measured: the GPU token path, prompt processing, reuse of processed prompts, copying from the context, the draft model, the checkpoint's native formats, and how the engine is tested against the reference implementation.

The workspace has two crates: the engine as a library (rustling, at the root), and the rustling command (rustling-cli, in cli/), which uses only the library's public API.

src/          the library
  engine/     the model thread: requests in, events out, the prompt cache kept
  generate/   sessions, sampling, copying, the draft model, the prompt cache
  model/      the layers and the state they keep
  gpu/        Metal: kernels, prompt paths, shaders
  weights/    checkpoint and GGUF formats, downloads
cli/src/      the command
  cli/        the commands
  server/     the HTTP API, over the engine

Development

cargo test --release          # the tests that need a model skip when it is not downloaded
uv run tools/golden.py --help # reference outputs from the transformers implementation

Privacy

rustling contacts the Hugging Face Hub to download models and nothing else. The Hub client's usage reporting is turned off.

Licence

Licensed under either of the Apache License, Version 2.0 or the MIT license, at your option. Contributions are accepted under the same terms.

The model has its own licence; see its model card.

Acknowledgements

The model is by Thinking Machines. The GGUF formats and the idea of copying from the context come from llama.cpp, which was also the yardstick for speed.

content_html_zh:
A fast local inference engine for Inkling 2 Mini on Apple silicon, written in Rust and built for coding agents. It serves an OpenAI-compatible API that Codex, aider and opencode can use as they would a hosted model.

It runs one model family and does not try to be general. That is what lets it do things a general engine does not: generate whole tokens in one GPU submission, keep processed prompts between requests and restarts, and copy runs of tokens the reply repeats from the conversation.

An earlier version of rustling chat running on an M1 Max with 64 GB. Watch it on asciinema.

要求

  • An Apple silicon Mac. Nothing else is supported: the engine is built around Metal and tuned on these chips.
  • Memory: 16.6 GB for the model, 1 to 5 GB for a conversation depending on its length, and up to 15 GB more while a long prompt is being processed. Measured on a 64 GB machine. 48 GB is comfortable; on 32 GB long prompts will push the model's own pages out of memory and slow down.
  • A Rust toolchain to build it.

快速启动

cargo install --path cli
rustling chat

The first run downloads Unsloth’s UD-Q4_K_M conversion (16.6 GB) to the Hugging Face cache, where other tools that use the Hub will find it too. rustling pull does only that, if you would rather fetch it ahead. A download that is interrupted starts again from the beginning; on an unreliable connection, hf download unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF Inkling-2-Mini-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf can resume, and rustling finds the file it leaves.

To serve it to other programs:

rustling serve
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}],
  "reasoning_effort": "low", "stream": true
}'

Usage

Chat

Run rustling chat from a project directory to ask questions about its files. The built-in agent runs the model locally and asks before reading or searching. Chat controls, sessions and MCP setup.

One reply

rustling generate "Write a function that reverses a linked list." --effort low
rustling generate "Write a haiku about rivers." --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.95 --seed 1
rustling generate "What is 17 * 23?" --temperature 0     # always the most likely token
rustling generate "Hello" --timing                       # where the time went

服务器

rustling serve                                           # http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
rustling serve --port 9000 --host 0.0.0.0                # reachable from other machines
rustling serve --context 32768 --max-tokens 8192         # a larger window and longer replies
rustling serve --cache-gb 16                             # keep up to 16 GiB of processed prompts
rustling serve --cache-dir /Volumes/fast/rustling        # keep them somewhere else
rustling serve --no-cache-dir                            # keep them in memory only
rustling serve --no-reasoning                            # disable reasoning for every request
rustling serve --temperature 0.2 --top-p 0.9             # sampling for requests that do not set their own
rustling serve --log-level debug                         # also report progress through long prompts

The server's flags are defaults. A request sets its own temperature, top_p, top_k, seed, max_tokens and stop, and its reasoning effort, which is not a server flag:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Is 91 prime?"}],
  "reasoning_effort": "high", "max_tokens": 2000
}'

Reasoning comes back as reasoning_content, apart from the answer. GET /v1/models names the model and GET /health says the server is up.

型号

rustling pull                                            # fetch the default model ahead of time
rustling pull thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini            # the published checkpoint, 19 GB
rustling chat --model thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini    # run it
rustling serve --model ~/models/Inkling-2-Mini-Q4_K_M.gguf   # a file you already have
RUSTLING_MODEL=thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini rustling chat # or by environment

Without the GPU

rustling chat --backend cpu
rustling pull --draft && rustling chat --backend cpu --draft   # the draft model helps on the CPU

编码剂

rustling serve provides streaming and tool calls through the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs. Configure Codex, aider or opencode.

表现

On a 64 GB M4 Max with a 40-core GPU, rustling and llama.cpp ran the default Unsloth UD-Q4_K_M model on Metal. Each engine processed the same three prompts from scratch and generated 128 tokens per reply. The table shows medians across three runs per prompt, with greedy sampling and token copying disabled.

Measurement 引擎 30 input tokens 2,413 input tokens 15,194 input tokens
Prompt time (s) rustling 0.5 12.3 73.9
Prompt time (s) 调用.cpp 0.23 8.9 73.5
Generation (tokens/s) rustling 43.2 35.0 29.3
Generation (tokens/s) 调用.cpp 37.1 35.7 30.7

In an agent session, rustling can reuse the part of the conversation it has already processed. Replies that repeat earlier text can also benefit from token copying. For run ranges, reproduction commands, and earlier M1 Max and M4 Max results with the LM Studio model, see the full benchmark results.

To try experimental split attention for long-context GGUF generation, build with cargo build --release --features split-attention and run target/release/rustling with a context window large enough for the prompt and reply (for example, serve --context 65536). It splits full attention across blocks of cached keys on the same GPU when generating one token with at least 32,768 visible keys. Prompt processing in large batches and speculative verification batches use the usual kernels. The different order of floating-point sums can change a reply.

准确性

The LM Studio Q4_K_M conversion was used for the measurements below. The GPU computes in a different arithmetic from the CPU, so each way of running it was scored against the published checkpoint: how often it picks the same most likely next token. The first row is the checkpoint itself in another, equally valid arithmetic, which shows how much disagreement is ordinary.

Source code (7,857 tokens) Agent session (12,891 tokens) The model's own writing in it
Checkpoint, float arithmetic 92.0% 87.0% 99.4%
Q4_K_M on the CPU 90.4% 83.7% 98.8%
Q4_K_M, GPU prompt path 90.6% 83.7% 98.8%
Q4_K_M, GPU token by token (last 2,600 tokens) 91.7% 93.5% 98.8%

Where the checkpoint gives its choice a probability of 90% or more, every row agrees with it at least 98% of the time, and on the model's own writing none of them ever disagreed. Perplexity is the same to within 2%. The conversion costs a point or two of agreement; running it on the GPU costs nothing measurable beyond that. tests/quality.rs reproduces this on text of your choosing.

选项

Everything has a default; these are the ones worth knowing. rustling <command> --help lists the rest.

选项 默认 它的作用
--model unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF:Q4_K_M A model name, a .gguf file or a checkpoint directory. Names are downloaded when missing. Also $RUSTLING_MODEL.
--backend auto auto uses the GPU; cpu does not.
--context by chip, see below The most tokens a prompt and its reply may take together.
--最大令牌数 4096 The longest reply.
--no-reasoning reasoning on Never let the model reason before answering. --effort none only shortens it.
--draft off Use the model's draft model to propose several tokens at a time. Only helps when generating on the CPU; with the GPU it is not used.
--no-copying copying on Stop proposing tokens copied from the conversation.
--cache-gb 8 How many GiB of processed prompts to keep, in memory and again on disk (serve).
--cache-dir, --no-cache-dir ~/.cache/rustling Where they are kept between runs, or not to keep them (serve).
--threads performance cores Worker threads for the CPU's share of the work.
--log-level info What is reported on stderr. Also $RUSTLING_LOG.

上下文窗口

The model takes up to 1,048,576 tokens, but time grows with the context, so the default is sized for the chip: a prompt that fills the window should still be processed in about two minutes.

Chip Default window
M1 16,384
M2 20,480
M3 24,576
M4 32,768
M5 40,960
还要别的吗 16,384

Only the M1 figure is measured (on an M1 Max). The others scale it by each generation's GPU and are estimates; measurements are welcome. --context sets any size you like. Each token of context costs 64 KB of memory, on top of a fixed 0.3 GB.

A prompt that does not fit is refused with a message saying so, and a reply stops when the window is full.

记录

Logs go to stderr through tracing. At info, the server reports each request: the size of its prompt, how much of it was reused, how long the rest took and at what speed, and the reply's length and speed in tokens per second.

[3] 8 messages, 11 tools, 12891 prompt tokens
[3] prompt: 12615 tokens reused, 276 processed in 5.7s (48 tokens/s)
[3] reply: 164 tokens in 8.5s (19.4 tokens/s), stop; copied: 3 of 21 proposed tokens accepted in 10 rounds

--log-level debug adds progress through long prompts, warn keeps only problems, and off is silent.

型号

Model Size Notes
unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF:Q4_K_M 16.6 GB The default. Uses Unsloth’s Inkling-2-Mini-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf on Metal or CPU.
lmstudio-community/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF:Q4_K_M 17.5 GB The previous default, selectable with --model.
thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini 19 GB The published checkpoint in its own formats, on the CPU with GPU help for long prompts. About 10 tokens/s. The reference for accuracy.
thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research The variable-loop research checkpoint; --passes picks how many times the looped layers run.

The GGUF loader reads F32, BF16, NVFP4, Q4_K, Q5_0, Q5_K, Q6_K and Q8_0 tensors.

限制

  • 仅文本。 The model's vision tower is not implemented.
  • One request at a time; others queue.
  • Apple silicon only. There is no CUDA or Vulkan backend, and none is planned.
  • A 4-bit conversion is a lossy copy of the checkpoint. See Accuracy for how close.

它是如何运作的

docs/internals.md describes each part and what it measured: the GPU token path, prompt processing, reuse of processed prompts, copying from the context, the draft model, the checkpoint's native formats, and how the engine is tested against the reference implementation.

The workspace has two crates: the engine as a library (rustling, at the root), and the rustling command (rustling-cli, in cli/), which uses only the library's public API.

src/          the library
  engine/     the model thread: requests in, events out, the prompt cache kept
  generate/   sessions, sampling, copying, the draft model, the prompt cache
  model/      the layers and the state they keep
  gpu/        Metal: kernels, prompt paths, shaders
  weights/    checkpoint and GGUF formats, downloads
cli/src/      the command
  cli/        the commands
  server/     the HTTP API, over the engine

发展

cargo test --release          # the tests that need a model skip when it is not downloaded
uv run tools/golden.py --help # reference outputs from the transformers implementation

隐私

rustling contacts the Hugging Face Hub to download models and nothing else. The Hub client's usage reporting is turned off.

The model has its own licence; see its model card.

致谢

The model is by Thinking Machines. The GGUF formats and the idea of copying from the context come from llama.cpp, which was also the yardstick for speed.
